newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Assembly elects Fabius as speaker.
newsitem.headline: French Assembly elects Fabius as speaker.

text.p: France's National Assembly elected Socialist former prime minister Laurent Fabius, 50, as speaker on Thursday in its first session since the left swept to power last week.
Fabius, who served as prime minister in 1984-86 and speaker in 1988-93, was elected with 290 votes to 223 for Gaullist Nicole Cathala.

Fabius was elected in the second round of voting after initially failing to win more than half the votes in the 577-seat assembly. He succeeds conservative Philippe Seguin who has now become the floor leader of the Gaullist RPR party.
Fabius was France's youngest prime minister of modern times when he was appointed at the age of 37 by the late president Francois Mitterrand.

His career in the past few years has been clouded by a scandal over AIDS-tainted blood products which were distributed by public health agencies while he was in power in the mid-1980s and infected 1,250 haemophiliacs.

A special court is investigating whether he should be brought to trial on charges of poisoning together with his former ministers of health and social affairs, Edmond Herve and Georgina Dufoix. The prosecutor in the Court of Justice of the Republic has recommended clearing all three.
